question: Does the two-step claim instrument (step 1 v5c sorts restatement / new claim, step 2 v5j judges only the new specifics) drop the false positives of the R1 fired claims and keep the stored violations, on a pool that is out of sample for both steps?
shaped_on_pools_note: the S279 pool file (286 held-out R1-fired claims), sha256 first 16 hex as fresh_pool writes excluded_pools; a live run needs a fresh manifest that excludes it or a train-split pool
pool: fresh: R1 (gpt-6-luna-openai extraction, prompt v1) fired claims on pieces outside the S279 pool and outside every claim of the runs above, labelled by the agent panel sheet (fresh_pool.py); the stored label wins only when it agrees with the panel majority, a disagreement is left out
subset: instrument_eval.select: half false positives (paraphrase, verbatim, background in proportion), half stored violations in proportion per writer, claim-hash order
verdict_rule: a claim is cleared when the step-1 majority is restatement; otherwise its verdict is the step-2 majority (unsupported = flagged, none = unverified); go needs every bar below
stop_rule: one gated run; a no_go is read at $0 with the stored reasons and is never re-run on the same pool with a changed prompt
stop_rule_enforced: two_step run --limit refuses when shared.llm_call_log (stage adhoc_aa1048) holds a gated run of this id, or of the same step-1 prompt on the same pool, or cannot be read; every ledger row of a run carries prereg, run_kind and pool
